purpose: Section 30 requires this artifact as part of the Path-B artifact set. Unlike its name suggests in the success case, this artifact does NOT certify or freeze REPLACEMENT_RUBRIC_V2 as a validated, reproducible methodology - the holdout re-test (17) failed the detailed-agreement gate. This artifact instead formally records the DISPOSITION of the one permitted redesign attempt: what was tried, what the holdout showed, and that it is NOT adopted as authoritative.
whatWasAttempted: REPLACEMENT_RUBRIC_V2 (_taxonomy-operational-rubric-v2-REPLACEMENT.json, hash sha256:e7f41b24b9b0e324a091747165dd197fd2b8f7eaed03b68b1eb0c0f952fe4fe2) - the ONE evidence-backed redesign permitted this phase per 15-ontology-redesign.json - added two precision clarifications (LOCATION_SCOPING_RULE_FOR_COMPOSITE_CLAIMS, SIBLING_ADJACENCY_RULE_FOR_TEXTUAL_OVERLAP) to the original rubric (06) without merging, splitting, or renaming any of the 12 taxonomy states.
holdoutResult: FAILED. Binary inter-reviewer agreement gate passed (96.97% >= 90%, though with a chance-adjustment caveat - see 17's mandatory kappa disclosure). Detailed inter-reviewer agreement gate FAILED (69.70% vs the required 85%) - WORSE than the original 65-case study's 76.67%, not better. A new, previously-unobserved confusable pair (INCOMPARABLE vs DISCOVERED_ONLY, driven by CONMED's blank-excerpt/description-only ground-truth authoring convention) emerged and was not addressed by the redesign, since the redesign was targeted at the two mechanisms confirmed BEFORE the holdout was drawn (chapeau/composite location-scoping and sibling-adjacency), not this third one.
decisionPerSection20: Per Section 20's explicit instruction - 'if the replacement ALSO fails reproducibility, STOP - do not design ontology V3 - return NEEDS_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION and fail the phase' - NO second redesign (a V3 rubric, or a state-count ontology simplification) is attempted in this phase. REPLACEMENT_RUBRIC_V2 is preserved in the repository as a historical artifact of the one permitted attempt, but is NOT adopted as Headroom's authoritative evaluation taxonomy going forward, and is NOT used to certify any comparison of V2's output against a 'ground truth' consensus (see 19-v2-vs-independent-consensus.json for what remains legitimately reportable).
whatThisMeansForTheOriginalRubric: 06-taxonomy-operational-rubric.json (the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign rubric) remains the last rubric that was actually validated against real evidence (the original 65-case study) - it is also not certified as reproducible (it failed the same detailed gate, 76.67%), but between the two, neither the original nor the replacement rubric achieves the required detailed reproducibility. Both are preserved as evidence for the architecture decision required in 25-final-verdict.json.
